document_metadata.document_title: Maine Stormwater Management Design Manual, Volume III

design_criteria.water_quality_volume_method: Treat the first 1 inch of runoff from impervious surfaces and 0.4 inch from landscaped areas.

evidence.excerpt: City of Portland ME MS4 follows Maine Stormwater Design Manual Vol III
An underdrained soil filter must detain and filter a runoff volume equal to 1.0 inch times the subcatchment's impervious area plus 0.4 inch times the subcatchment's landscaped developed area.
A filter basin must drain dry in no less than 24 and no more than 48 hours.
The bottom of the constructed basin, including any underdrain soil filters should be one (1) foot above the seasonal high groundwater table
The bottom of the underdrained soil filter should be a minimum of 18 inches above the seasonal high groundwater table or bedrock
The soil filter over the gravel underdrain pipe bedding must be at least 18 inches deep
The peak water quality storage depth should not exceed 6 inches over a bioretention basin filter.
Provide a long and narrow basin shape, with a minimum 2:1 length to width ratio (3:1 is best).
Roof Slope: A minimum slope of 2% is considered normal for extensive and simple intensive greening.
The target detention time for the treatment volume should be between 24 to 48 hours.
Recommended infiltration should be less than 2.41 inches per hour but great enough that one inch of stored precipitation infiltrates in 24 hours (i.e. >0.04 inches per hour).

extraction_quality.review_notes: Municipality coverage via Maine Vol III (Augusta pattern).

design_parameters.enrich_notes: WQv sizing uses 1.0 inch over impervious area plus 0.4 inch over landscaped/developed vegetated area (Volume III Ch. 7). Underdrained vegetated soil filters require 18 inches minimum separation from seasonal high water table or bedrock; many other BMPs specify 1 foot (12 inches). Filter and gravel-wetland drawdown targets are 24–48 hours; detention basins should be dry within 2–3 days. Wet pond plug-flow shape minimum L:W is 2:1 (3:1 preferred). Pervious surfaces cite infiltration test bounds (<2.41 in/hr and >0.04 in/hr) and 8-inch minimum pretreatment filter layer; proprietary pretreatment uses Maine DEP Appendix B approval letters, not TAPE/NJCAT.
